2025 was a year of learning for me. Learning what drained me, what supported me, and where I was moving through life without much intention. 

It wasn’t a bad year, but it was a full one. A year of adjusting, figuring things out as I went, and realizing that I can’t keep pouring my energy everywhere and expect to feel grounded.

As I start thinking about 2026, I didn’t want another year that just happens to me. I wanted to go into it with clarity. With goals that feel realistic. With intentions that actually support the life I’m living and not an ideal version of it.

That’s why this reset looks the way it does.

A new journal. A new planner. Clearer routines. More boundaries. Less rushing. More presence.

I also created these prompts because I know I’m not the only one who feels this way. So many of us end the year tired, overwhelmed, and unsure where to even start. 

These questions aren’t about perfection or a glow-up. They are about slowing down, getting honest, and choosing what you want more of and what you’re ready to leave behind.

My hope is that these prompts help guide you into a year that feels calmer, more intentional, and more aligned with who you’re becoming. A year where you’re not just setting goals, but building a life that actually feels good to live.

Here’s to entering 2026 with clarity, purpose, and a little more grace for ourselves 🤍

31 days of journaling prompts for December🎄

It’s time to reflect on 2026 and prepare for the new year and the best way to do that is through journaling. 

I’ve found that planning for January goes better when you reflect on what happened, so spend the first half of the month looking back at what this year was like and what you’re still carrying and then for the second half focus on what you want next.

That’s what these journaling prompts are for. Every day in December, answer one question in your journal, to help you close out the year and start thinking about the next one from a calmer place.

This will help you step into the new year knowing what you actually want from it, so the plans you make come from reflection rather than the pressure to start fresh.

Save this post and come back to one prompt each day throughout December.

30 days of journaling prompts for November 🍂

Every November I like to start looking ahead, but in order to do so successfully, we need to look at the year we’re still in. 

You don’t always need a vision board or a long list of goals, or resolutions, but start with looking back honestly at what this year actually was. Get curious about where you are now and why. 

What did you set out to do in January and what happened to it? Maybe there were things you wanted to do, but ended up putting off again, ask yourself why. 

That’s what these journaling prompts are for. Every day in November, answer one question in your journal, to help you reflect on the past year, understand why some things didn’t happen and get clear on what you want to bring into the new year.

This will help you understand your year a little better, so the goals you set next can be based on what’s true for you, not on what you think you should want.

Save this post and come back to one prompt each day throughout November.

7 steps to hard reset your life before the year ends
7 steps to hard reset your life before 2027

If you’ve been feeling a little all over the place lately, here’s your sign to do a hard reset. 

Give yourself the next 30 days ❤️

Before you start making million goals, you should ask yourself much simpler questions first:

How is your life actually going rn?

You can see I used a scheme here but you can use any criteria or systems you would like in order to have a visual representation of where you at. 

I’m not saying a clean room will fix everything but your environment takes up mental space. 

This reset starts with a trash bag. 

No one prepared me for the fact that being an adult means having to answer “what are we eating?” - approximately 21 times a week.

Having even a loose idea of what I’m going to eat and what I need from the grocery store saves me SO much mental energy. 

Tick that off your schedule at the beginning of the week 

Make a list of the habits, behaviors and little patterns you know you don’t want to take with you.

You definitely need fewer things draining you.

Close all the open tabs in your brain. 

And finally, once you’ve cleared some space, you get to decide what you’re actually making space for. 

You don’t become a new person in one day.
You become them through the little things you repeatedly do.

HOW TO FALL IN LOVE WITH YOUR LIFE AGAIN. ❤️

What if the life you're dreaming of starts with appreciating the life you already have?

Sometimes, we become so focused on achieving more, earning more, and becoming better that we forget to enjoy the life we're living right now.

Falling in love with your life again doesn't mean everything has to be perfect. It means learning to find happiness in the smallest moments.

✨ 1. Stop comparing your journey. Your timeline is different. Trust it.

🌱 2. Celebrate small wins. Every little step forward matters.

☀️ 3. Romanticize your everyday life. Enjoy your morning coffee, favourite music, peaceful walks, and quiet moments.

📖 4. Invest in yourself. Read books, learn new skills, and challenge your limits.

🧠 5. Protect your peace. Stop giving your energy to things you cannot control.

❤️ 6. Spend time with people who inspire you. Surround yourself with positive energy.

🔥 7. Create a life you're excited to wake up to. Build habits, follow your passions, and work towards meaningful goals.

Remember, life isn't just about reaching the destination. It's also about enjoying every little moment along the way.

You don't need a new life to feel happy. Sometimes, you just need a new perspective.

Fall in love with your life, one day at a time.

Save this reminder for the days you forget how beautiful life can be. ❤️
